Information since the March meeting supports holding the funds rate at 2.25–2.50 percent with a patient, neutral-to-dovish bias: the labor market remains strong, activity solid, and 12-month inflation below 2 percent; setting IOER at 2.35 percent is a technical adjustment, not hawkish.

SLOOS cross-check (April 2019) adds a note of caution: banks tightened standards for C&I and construction/land development loans and tightened other terms broadly; demand weakened for HELOCs, credit cards, and other consumer loans, with demand unchanged for auto and subprime mortgages. This points to some softening in credit availability and demand, modestly tempering the near-term growth tone and reinforcing a patient/dovish policy stance.

Financial Stability Report context: easier market conditions early 2019 support risk sentiment, but elevated valuations and high business leverage remain vulnerabilities. Overall: mildly positive activity backdrop with a neutral-to-dovish policy bias, but more cautious given tightening credit conditions in SLOOS.
